Puzzle 679 Prime-proof odd integers

Problems & Puzzles: Puzzles

Puzzle 679 Prime-proof odd integers

“Prime-proof odd integers” are odd composite numbers not ending in 5 that remain composite even when a single decimal digit of the number is changed.

For the origins of these numbers see: 1 & 2

Q. Can you find palindrome-Prime-proof odd integers other than : 707696707 and 998020899?

Contributions came from Giovanni Resta, Vicente Felipe, J. K. Andersen, Hakan Summakoglu & Emmanuel Vanteighem.

***

Giovanni Resta wrote:

there are quite a lot of these numbers.

Up to 10^15 I counted 2078 of them.

In this range, the first are

707696707, 998020899, 13753335731, 31776967713, 32782028723

and the last are

998980717089899, 999183464381999, 999222626222999.

The first such numbers made only of zeros and ones are

101110100111001011101 and 1111011011001001001001101101111.

The smallest such number with 100 digits is

100000000000000000000000000000000000000000000219099091200000

0000000000000000000000000000000000000001.

J. K. Andersen wrote:

The next examples: 13753335731, 31776967713, 33215451233, 39571617593.

A 2013-digit example: (10^2013-1)/9 + 65161816156*10^1001.

***

Hakan Summakoglu wrote:

I tested integers <10^13 and found 189 palindrome-prime-proof odd integers.

There are 2 palindromes with 9 digits, 17 palindromes with 11 digits, 7 palindromes with 12 digits,

163 palindromes with 13 digits. Interestingly; 2,17,7,163 are prime numbers.

There are 2 palindromes with 9 digits:

707696707, 998020899
